subject.title: Text between tool calls leaks to messaging channels

question: Should external source chats keep automatic visible final-text delivery as the compatibility default while adding narrower leak suppression, or should OpenClaw move them to message-tool/final-only delivery by default?
rationale: The secure boundary and the documented default pull in different directions: keeping automatic delivery preserves existing replies but leaves more responsibility on phase/classification guards, while switching defaults can stop leaks but break current channel behavior.

options.title: Preserve default, harden boundary
options.body: Keep documented automatic final replies as the default and add generic suppression for internal, commentary, reasoning, and inter-tool payloads before any channel or cron delivery path.

options.title: Move to explicit sends
options.body: Change external source chats to message-tool/final-only delivery by default with a documented migration or doctor guidance for users who need legacy automatic replies.

options.title: Accept opt-in mitigations only
options.body: Land opt-in controls such as final-tag enforcement but leave the issue open because default external-channel leakage would remain possible.

recommendation.title: Preserve default, harden boundary
recommendation.body: Keep documented automatic final replies as the default and add generic suppression for internal, commentary, reasoning, and inter-tool payloads before any channel or cron delivery path.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans source reply defaults, agent commentary suppression, and security/product compatibility, where steipete has the strongest recent history in this evidence set.
